title: Afternoon Walk & Café
setting:
An afternoon walk with Heli through a neighborhood park after the gym. They talk about the workout, notice things along the way, and end up stopping at a café.

---
goal: Use city and nature vocabulary (park, tree, dog, building, store, bench, bridge) without hesitating
Talk about the gym and how you feel in a natural, flowing way
Order at a café and handle the bill comfortably

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: My legs are so tired. I don't know why I agreed to walk after the gym.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Because the weather is nice. Look at that park over there.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: There's a bench near the bridge. Do you want to sit for a minute?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: No, let's keep going. We can rest at the café.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: Look at that dog. It's running so fast.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Yes, its owner is trying to catch up with it.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: Those trees are beautiful.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Yes. And look at the building behind them — I think it's new.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: There are so many stores on this street.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Yes. I want to look at that one later.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: You looked strong at the gym this morning.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: I don't feel strong right now. I'm very tired.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: Me too. But we ran for twenty minutes — that's not bad.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: True. But my legs feel heavy now.

lines.speaker: Waiter
lines.text: Good afternoon. What can I get you?

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: I'd like a cappuccino and a piece of cake, please.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: An espresso, please. And do you have a table outside?

lines.speaker: Waiter
lines.text: Of course. Take any table you'd like.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Thank you. We'll take that one in the corner.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: That cake was really good.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Yes. Can we ask for the bill?

lines.speaker: Waiter
lines.text: Here is the bill. I hope you enjoyed everything.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: Yes, thank you. Should we leave a tip?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Of course. The service was good. I'll add it when I pay.

title: Sunday Morning at Home
setting:
A Sunday morning at home. Mark woke up with back pain and tells Heli over coffee. They talk about it briefly and make plans for the day — they need cash and have a small transfer to do, so they decide to head to the ATM together. Because Mark's back hurts, Heli suggests taking a taxi.

---
goal: Use health vocabulary (pain, back, hurt, feel) without hesitating when something is wrong
Handle a simple bank errand in conversation — cash, transfer, receipt — naturally
Maintain flow when moving between topics in a casual home conversation

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: Good morning. How are you feeling?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Not well. I have pain in my back.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: Did you hurt it yesterday at the gym?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: I think so. I don't feel well this morning.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: Take some medicine. There's some in the kitchen.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Yes, I'll take it now.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: We need to go to the ATM today — we have no cash at home.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Okay. How much do you want me to take out?

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: About five hundred shekels. Can you also transfer some money to my account?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Yes, I'll do that too. I'll use my card at the ATM.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: Should we take a taxi? Your back still hurts.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Yes, good idea. I'll call a taxi now.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: Tell the driver the address — the bank near the main road.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Okay. And I'll ask for a receipt this time.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: Good. Don't forget to sign when you transfer.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: I know. I'll pay and then we can go home.

title: At the Ice Rink
setting:
An evening at the ice rink with Heli. They check in, sort out the locker, skate for a while, and take a break when Mark's leg starts hurting.

---
goal: Use skating and gym vocabulary (skates, locker, membership, bottle) without hesitating
Talk about how you feel physically in a natural, flowing way
Handle a simple check-in at a desk and move on without breaking the conversation

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: This ice rink is busier than last week.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Yes. But there's still enough space to skate.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: Let's find a locker first.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: I'll go ask at the desk — I'm not sure if our membership is still valid.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Excuse me — is our membership still valid?

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: Yes, until the end of the month. Do you need a locker?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Yes please, thank you.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: I put the bottles in the locker.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Good. Let's put our skates on and get on the ice.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: You're going very fast. Slow down a little.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: I'm fine. I like to skate fast.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: You look so strong today.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: I don't feel strong. I'm already tired.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: Already? We've only been skating for twenty minutes.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: I know. My legs are still tired from yesterday.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: Let's take a break and drink something.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Yes — my bottle is in the locker.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: How are your legs feeling now?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: I have a little pain in my right leg.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: Then let's rest for a bit. Sit down here.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Okay. Maybe ten minutes and then we can skate again.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: Should we renew the membership next month?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Yes. What's the price now?

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: I think it went up a little. I'll check.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Okay. Let's do it before we leave today.

title: Saturday DIY at Home
setting:
A Saturday afternoon at home. Mark has laid out the tools to put up a new shelf in the living room. Heli helps — holding the ladder, handing tools over, and doing a small paint touch-up on the wall around the shelf. Somewhere in the middle they take a coffee break.

---
goal: Use home and tools vocabulary — shelf, hammer, screws, glue, brush — without hesitating
Handle short requests and instructions naturally — "can you hold this", "pass me the..."
Talk about what you're doing and what comes next with simple present and future tense

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: I put the box with the tools in the living room. Is that where you want to work?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Yes, perfect. I want to start with the shelf.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: This shelf is really heavy. Can you carry it?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Yes. Can you hold the other end?

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: What do you need first — the hammer or the screws?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Both, please.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: The battery in the clock is dead. Can you change it too?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Yes, I have extra batteries in the box.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: Do you need me to hold the shelf while you fix it?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Yes please. Hold it straight.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: You'll need the ladder to reach up there.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: I know. Can you hold the ladder for me?

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: Be careful on the ladder. Your neck will start hurting.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: You're right. I can already feel it a little.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: Should we use glue here or just the screws?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Just the screws — they're enough.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: The wall needs a little paint around the shelf. Can you pass me the brush?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Here. I'll clean the wall first. Then we can paint.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: Where did you put the ladder? I need to move it.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: I put the ladder back against the wall in the hallway.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: Let's take a break. I'll make coffee.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Good idea. I'm tired — that shelf was really heavy.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: Is your neck still okay? You were on the ladder for a while.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: My neck is fine. I was careful.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: Did you put the tools back in the box?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Not yet. I'll do it after coffee.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: Do you want to go to the store after this? I need a few things.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Sure. I just need to clean up first.

title: A Walk Through a New Neighborhood
setting:
A Saturday afternoon walk through a Tel Aviv neighborhood Mark and Heli don't usually visit. Mark has just had his second physio session and is feeling noticeably better. Heli asks how he's doing as they walk, and they talk while noticing things around the city.

---
goal: Use city vocabulary — traffic light, pedestrian, bicycle, bridge, fence, turn — without hesitating
Give a health update naturally — shoulder, neck, inflammation, muscle — without stopping to think
Use past tense and cause-effect chains naturally in casual conversation
notes: Felt natural overall. Heli flagged that the practice sessions have become repetitive — health/physio topics appear too frequently in consecutive sessions. Returning to a subject after a break is fine, but back-to-back sessions with the same theme wear thin. Future practice sessions should vary the subject more deliberately, even when recent lessons have been health-focused.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: You're walking so much more freely today. Is the inflammation going down?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Yes — a lot. The shoulder feels almost normal.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: And your neck? You had so much pain there last week.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Yes, it was much worse last week. Now I can move it without thinking about it.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: Let's turn right here — I think there's more to see this way.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Okay. There's a traffic light ahead. We can cross there.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: Look how different this part of the city is.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Yes — and look at all the pedestrians and bicycles. There are so many people here.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: There's a bridge over there. I've never walked across it.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Let's go. I see a nice old fence along the path.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: There's a park on the other side. Do you want to walk through it?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Yes. Let's go through the park and then head back slowly.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: Did the physiotherapist give you new exercises this time?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Yes. She showed me some for the neck — I need to do them twice a day.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: And the muscle in your shoulder — is there still pain?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Not really. The muscle feels much better than last week.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: It sounds like things are going much better this time.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Yes — the inflammation is almost gone. I can feel the difference.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: As long as you keep doing the exercises.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: I will. She said that without the exercises, the inflammation comes back.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: Should we stop somewhere after the park? There's usually a market around here on Saturdays.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Good idea. Let's see what they have.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: It's past the park — we turn left after the bridge.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Okay. Let's go.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: I'm really glad you're feeling better. The inflammation was so bad last week.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: I know. But I'm fine now. Let's keep going.

title: Saturday Lunch
setting:
Mark and Heli go out for Saturday lunch at a Tel Aviv café they've been to before. Heli made a reservation. The scene runs from arrival to paying the bill, with the easy back-and-forth a couple has when eating out together.

---
goal: Order a meal and interact with a waiter naturally without stopping to think
Use restaurant vocabulary — soup, salad, menu, bill, tip — without hesitating
Make recommendations and simple requests in a service setting with no gaps

lines.speaker: Waiter
lines.text: Welcome! Do you have a reservation?

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: Yes, for two — under Heli.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Is our table ready?

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: Our table is nice — right next to the window.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Yes. Can you pass me the menu?

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: I made the reservation for one o'clock. We're exactly on time.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Good. Last time we had to wait a long time.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: Have you been here before? What do you recommend?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: I recommend the soup — I ordered it last time and it was really good.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: I'll have the salad then. Soup and a sandwich for you?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Yes, and a decaf to finish.

lines.speaker: Waiter
lines.text: Are you ready to order?

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: Yes. The salad for me, please, and a cappuccino.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: And the soup for me. With a sandwich and a decaf, please.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: I love this place — it's never too busy on a Saturday.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: I know. Last time we came in the evening and had to wait outside.

lines.speaker: Waiter
lines.text: The soup and the salad. Enjoy!

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: Thank you. Could we have some bread too?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Thank you. This looks really good.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: How's the soup?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Really good. You should try it next time.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: Is the decaf okay here? Last time mine was too strong.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: It's fine — exactly how I like it.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: Should we ask the waiter to recommend a dessert?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Yes, good idea. I'll ask.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Excuse me — what do you recommend for dessert?

lines.speaker: Waiter
lines.text: The chocolate cake is very popular today.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Perfect, we'll take one. For the two of us.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: Should we make a reservation for next week too?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Good idea. I'll make the reservation when we leave.

lines.speaker: Waiter
lines.text: Here is the bill. I hope you enjoyed everything.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: Yes, it was great. Should we leave a tip?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Of course. I'll pay by card.

title: Morning at the Gym
setting:
A weekday morning at the gym. Heli has the morning free and joins Mark for a workout. They talk at the lockers when they arrive, during the warm-up, briefly mid-workout at the weights, and over a water break on the bench. Near the end they make plans for the ice rink in the evening.

---
goal: Use gym vocabulary — warm-up, weights, treadmill, locker — without hesitating
Talk about a workout naturally — running, lifting, resting, training — without stopping to think
Keep up casual conversation mid-workout with short, natural sentences

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: Did you take a locker near the entrance? Mine is a bit far.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Yes — I took one next to the door. Easier after the workout.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: Should we do a warm-up first? I always skip it and then my muscles hurt.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Yes, good idea. Let's do five minutes.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: After the warm-up, I'm going to the weights. Are you coming?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Not yet — I want to run first.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: How fast are you going to run?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Not too fast. I just want to get moving.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: You're lifting more than last time. It looks heavy.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: A little. But my muscles are handling it.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: How long do you usually train on a weekday?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: About an hour. I like to train in the morning when it's quiet.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: I need a break. Where did you put the bottle?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: It's on the bench near the treadmill. I'll rest for a minute too.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: You skipped half your warm-up earlier — I saw you.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Only half. I did a short warm-up on the treadmill first.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: Come join me at the weights when you're done resting.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Almost done. I'll come to the weights in a minute.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: What's your favorite exercise here?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Probably running. I like to run fast for a few minutes at the end.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: Are we still going to the ice rink tonight?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Yes — I want to skate a little. I haven't been in two weeks.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: Are you tired? We can leave after this set.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: A little. One more round, then I'm done.

title: Planning the Day
setting:
Saturday morning at the kitchen table. Mark and Heli are having coffee and making a plan for the day — stop at the ATM, do some food shopping, and make a dinner reservation for the evening. The conversation runs from the first coffee to walking out the door.

---
goal: Make plans and discuss logistics naturally — bank, store, dinner — without stopping to think
Use future tense and time expressions smoothly in everyday planning conversation
Keep the back-and-forth flowing without gaps when deciding what to do next

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: Do you want an espresso? I'm making one.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Yes please. With a little milk.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: What do we need to do today?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: I want to go to the bank first. Then the store.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: Are you going inside or just the ATM?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Just the ATM — I need to withdraw some cash.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: Should we check our savings while we're there?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Yes — good idea. I haven't been to the bank in a while.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: The roads are always busy on Saturday morning.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: I know. Let's leave early to avoid the traffic.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: Should we drive or walk?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Let's drive — there's too much to carry from the store.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: Don't forget to take the receipt at the store.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: I won't. I want to check the price of a few things too.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: The store will probably be crowded too.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Then let's go early — it'll be less busy in the morning.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: Should we make a reservation somewhere for tonight?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Good idea. Where do you want to go?

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: Let's decide now so we can book before we leave.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Okay. I'll make the reservation for eight o'clock.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: How much cash do you want to take out?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Not sure yet — I want to check our savings first.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: Okay. Finish your espresso and let's go.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: One more minute. I'm almost done.
